Subject: Finova: Performance SLO + Regional Routing follow-up

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so we have a single source of truth: 

Call highlights / requirements
- Latency targets (p95): US (150ms), EU (200ms), APAC (250ms) for interactive generation paths.
- Throughput / concurrency: initial pilot ~200 concurrent users (burst to 1k), target steady throughput ~120 QPS for text generation endpoints.
- Streaming: customer UX requires token-by-token streaming for long responses (progressive render) and client-side cancellation support.
- Regional routing / data residency: user requests should be routed to region closest to user; EU training/PII must not leave EU (data residency constraint).
- Failover: automatic fallback to a compatible model in a different region is acceptable only for non-PII requests; for PII/EU-resident flows must remain in-region.

Next steps (owners / dates)
1) SLO + regional routing draft (attached): I'm sending a first-draft SLO proposal and regional routing options — please review. (Marissa) — today EOD.
2) Technical deep-dive with Aditya to confirm streaming & concurrency sizing, network checklist, and firewall requirements. (Aditya) — propose Tue 6/22.
3) Procurement contact and initial T&Cs review (Marcus) — will reach out with procurement packet. (Marcus) — by next Wed 6/24.
4) SOC2 / compliance evidence request: we'll attach SOC2 evidence and can discuss private deployment options if needed. (Marissa)

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (draft), network-topology.png (example routing), SOC2-evidence.xlsx (summary).

If anything above looks off, flag it and I'll update the doc. Otherwise, let me know availability for the technical deep-dive — Aditya suggested Tue 6/22 at 10am PT or Wed 6/23 at 9am PT.

Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the p95 targets look good as a starting point. For billing-critical flows we may ask for stricter p99 guarantees later.
- Streaming: yes, token-by-token streaming is a hard requirement for our customer chat flows; ability to cancel mid-generation is required.
- Regional routing: EU data residency is critical. For any requests touching customer PII we need assurance that both compute and logs remain in EU.
- Concurrency: our initial pilot volume estimate is ~200 concurrent active chat users, with potential bursts up to ~1k during peak marketing events.

Also: can you provide a short checklist we can drop into our infra team for firewall/VPN requirements? And an early cost ballpark — we need to show finance something before the procurement call.

I can do Tue 6/22 10am PT for the deep-dive.

Thanks Samir — quick technical responses and what we'll bring to the deep-dive: 

Streaming
- We support token-by-token streaming over chunked transfer / SSE for our generation endpoints; clients can call the cancel endpoint or close the connection to terminate early, and we will free KV cache resources. We'll include a sample client snippet in the deep-dive deck.

Concurrency / throughput sizing
- Pilot (200 concurrent chats): recommended to start on Dedicated capacity with 4 workers (NVIDIA H100-class or equivalent) giving headroom for batching and concurrency; this maps to ~120 QPS for the typical short-turn dialog.
- Bursts to 1k: autoscaling or burst into hosted tier; we typically recommend an autoscale policy + warm standby region.

Regional routing & residency
- Routing: we can route by X-User-Region header or IP-geolocation. For EU-residency flows we suggest a distinct endpoint (e.g., eu-api.redwood.ai) that guarantees compute and logs are in EU.
- Logs & telemetry: we can optionally disable audit-level telemetry for in-region flows and push logs to a customer-managed S3 in the EU to meet data residency controls (requires Private / VPC option).

Failover behavior
- By default we allow model-variant fallback across regions for non-PII requests. For PII-tagged requests we will honor an in-region-only policy and return a 503 if capacity is constrained (or route to a pre-provisioned dedicated pool).

Network checklist (summary)
- Outbound IPs to allow: 52.18.34.0/24, 34.206.12.0/24 (example) — we'll provide exact CIDRs in the checklist attachment.
- TLS mutual-auth option supported for Private deployments; otherwise TLS 1.2+ with client certs for sensitive flows.

Deliverables for deep-dive (we'll bring):
- Detailed SLO doc (Marissa)
- Network checklist + CIDRs (attached: network-topology.png)
- Concurrency sizing and capacity plan (this deck)

Attachments referenced: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (draft), network-topology.png

I'll prepare the client streaming snippet and run a short load-curve demo during the call. See you Tue 6/22 10am PT.
